Alex Kim: Hey team — quick onboarding question. I uploaded a marriage certificate to Rippling yesterday but my spouse still shows as 'dependent pending' for dental. I uploaded it under Personal Documents; is there a separate benefits upload folder?

Maya (People Ops): Hi @Alex Kim, welcome! Usually uploads to Personal Docs can work, but please upload again under Documents > Category: Benefits > Subtype: Dependent proof to ensure the Benefits Team picks it up quickly. We need either the marriage certificate or a joint tax return plus spouse SSN and DOB.

Alex Kim: Thanks — I did Personal Docs because I missed the category dropdown. Can you confirm the exact steps?

Luca (HR Systems): Sure — Rippling path: Rippling -> Documents -> Add Document. Choose Category: Benefits, Subtype: Dependent proof. Example filename: alex_kim_spouse_marriage_certificate.pdf. Also tick "Share with Benefits Team" when prompted.

Luca (HR Systems): Snippet: ```Rippling > Documents > Add Document > Category: Benefits > Subtype: Dependent proof```

Benefits Bot: Document received and queued for verification. Ticket #BZ-6123. Status: pending review. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Maya (People Ops): Once you re-upload we typically verify within 1-2 business days. After verification the dependent status flips and payroll deductions for dental will begin on the next pay cycle. If you're within 30 days of hire we can make coverage retroactive to your enrollment date; after 30 days it may be treated as a qualifying life event. If you're past 30 days DM me and we'll sort it.

Jordan (Payroll): FYI @Alex Kim — deductions will show as a payroll line item labeled "Dental - Employee + Dependent" on the paycheck following verification. If you tell me your pay period end date I can confirm which paycheck will reflect the change.

Alex Kim: I re-uploaded under Benefits and shared with the Benefits Team. The bot created ticket BZ-6123. Also, I had enrolled in FSA during open enrollment — do I need to change anything to have dependent dental expenses covered?

Maya (People Ops): If you want dependent dental in FSA, update elections at Rippling -> Benefits -> Manage Elections. Because adding a spouse is a qualifying life event, we've annotated your ticket to permit a midyear FSA election change. I'll follow up to confirm the change window and effective date.

Alex Kim: Perfect — I wasn't sure if FSA needed a separate doc. Appreciate the help.

Maya (People Ops): No problem. If verification seems delayed after 48 hours, ping me or email benefits@redwood.com with the ticket number. :thumbsup:

Alex Kim: Will do, thanks everyone!
